stories.statLabel: seats: Netanyahu bloc vs Eisenkot bloc
stories.headline: Israel's final count leaves both blocs short of a majority
body: With over 99% counted, Netanyahu's bloc has 53 seats and Eisenkot's opposition bloc 48, Haaretz reports.
Arab-led parties won a combined 19 seats.
Neither side reaches 61, and opposition leaders are meeting to explore a coalition.
stories.joke: Nobody won. Everyone's negotiating. Business as usual.
stories.vc: A long caretaker government delays Israel's budget and big policy calls.

stories.headline: US and Japan agree to build missiles together in Japan
body: The US and Japan will set up a Japanese plant to jointly produce advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles.
Japan's defence minister announced it at a regional meeting in the Philippines.
Both countries are worried about China's growing assertiveness.
stories.vc: Allied co-production is spreading defence manufacturing across Asia, a market Indian firms also want in.

stories.statLabel: cost of the Iran war so far
stories.headline: Pentagon says the Iran war has cost US taxpayers $47 billion
body: The Pentagon told Congress the war on Iran has cost at least $47.1 billion so far.
The figure came days before Tuesday's midterm elections.
Analysts say it could affect how some people vote.
stories.vc: War spending adds to US deficits, which pushes up borrowing costs worldwide.

image.credit: David B. Gleason from Chicago, IL / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Finland opens criminal probe into Google's data centre site
body: Finnish police are investigating whether a Google subsidiary broke environmental law at its planned data centre in Muhos.
It allegedly cleared and drained 330 hectares of forest before required impact assessments were done.
Locals reacted angrily to the tree felling.
stories.joke: Cloud computing, but first you have to remove the actual trees.
stories.vc: Data centre growth is running into local pushback everywhere; permits are now a real risk to AI build-out timelines.

stories.headline: Norway's tourist board answers a Trump insult with toilet tourism
body: After Trump called Norway a 'shithouse country' at a rally, Visit Norway showed off its loveliest public toilets.
The jibe followed his anger at not winning the Nobel peace prize.
The tourist board joked that Norway makes them 'great again'.
stories.joke: Best marketing team in Europe, flushed with success.
stories.vc: Quick, funny brand responses earn free global attention, the cheapest ad a tourist board can buy.

stories.headline: Shadowfax's quarterly profit jumps over 5x to ₹68 crore
body: Logistics firm Shadowfax's September-quarter profit rose to ₹68 crore from ₹13 crore a year earlier.
Revenue climbed 57% to a record ₹1,537.7 crore.
It was its sixth straight quarter of growth, the company said.
stories.vc: Profitable logistics players are riding quick commerce; listed peers will be judged against these margins.

stories.headline: Pine Labs' quarterly profit rises over 6x to ₹38.6 crore
body: Payments firm Pine Labs made ₹38.6 crore in the September quarter, up from ₹6 crore.
Revenue rose 24% to ₹806.2 crore.
Profit nearly doubled from the previous quarter.
stories.joke: Card machines: still beeping, now profitably.
stories.vc: Fintech listings that turn profitable support valuations for the next wave of payment IPOs.

stories.headline: Trucking platform BlackBuck's profit rises 42%
body: BlackBuck's September-quarter profit rose 41.8% to ₹41.4 crore.
Revenue jumped 55.7% to ₹235.3 crore.
A much lower tax bill helped; costs rose faster than revenue.
stories.joke: Trucks keep moving, and so does the bottom line.
stories.vc: Digitising India's fragmented trucking market is a large, slow prize; investors like steady profits here.

stories.headline: Justdial fined ₹10 lakh for listing explosive chemicals
body: The consumer protection authority fined Justdial for listing ammonium nitrate, a regulated hazardous substance.
It follows action against seven e-commerce platforms over explosive listings.
Justdial says it removed the listings and expects no other impact.
stories.joke: Search for 'explosive deals' and you got exactly that.
stories.vc: Platforms are being held responsible for what sellers list, raising compliance costs across e-commerce.

stories.headline: Bengaluru cancels and reissues elevated corridor tenders again
body: B-SMILE cancelled tenders for two elevated corridor projects and reissued them the same day at lower estimated costs.
They include Minerva Circle–Hudson Circle and Sholay Circle–St. John's Hospital on Hosur Road.
It cited technical reasons, on the urban development department's instruction.
stories.joke: Bengaluru infrastructure: now available in 'try again' mode.
stories.vc: Repeated tender resets delay projects and raise costs for contractors bidding on city infra.

stories.headline: GM pays $220 million over selling drivers' data
body: General Motors will pay $220 million to 36 US states over claims it sold driving and location data to brokers.
Brokers then sold it to insurers.
GM must now get drivers' express consent before collecting or sharing such data.
stories.joke: Your car knew you braked hard. So did your insurer.
stories.vc: Car data is valuable, but consent rules make selling it far harder, a hit to 'connected car' business models.

stories.headline: US probed a suspected Chinese spy close to Nvidia's CEO
body: The New York Times reports US agencies watched Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore AI cloud firm Megaspeed, for about a year.
Megaspeed was accused of illegally selling Nvidia chips to China.
Officials worried she was gathering information on Nvidia's plans.
stories.joke: Dinner with Jensen, dessert with intelligence agencies.
stories.vc: Chip export enforcement keeps tightening, which shapes where AI hardware can be sold.

stories.headline: Meta quietly tests an AI app that styles outfits from your closet
body: Meta's Style Sketch builds a virtual closet from your Instagram photos or pictures you add.
It suggests outfits and lets you try them on a model matched to your body shape and skin tone.
It is live in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand.
stories.joke: Finally, an app to tell you that shirt doesn't go with those trousers.
stories.vc: AI styling could become a powerful shopping funnel for Instagram's ads.

stories.headline: Dolores Huerta, champion of farmworkers' rights, dies at 96
body: Dolores Huerta, co-founder of the National Farm Workers Association, has died aged 96.
She coined 'Sí Se Puede' and spent over 70 years fighting for better pay and treatment for farmworkers.
She was known especially for her work for women farmworkers.
stories.vc: Her organising won wage and safety protections that still shape US farm labour costs.

image.credit: Office of Senator Kamala Harris / Wikimedia Commons

stories.statLabel: of Americans link data centres to energy bills
stories.headline: Women are leading the backlash against data centres
body: Women are at the front of a fast-growing, cross-party backlash to data centres, packing meetings and running for office.
Pew found half of Americans think data centres affect home energy costs.
Opposition is strongest among women, and some say it will shape their vote.
stories.joke: The AI boom met its toughest opponent: a local residents' meeting.
stories.vc: Local opposition can delay data centres for years, a growing risk for AI infrastructure investors.

stories.headline: South Korea plans to allow abortion pills, with tight limits
body: A South Korean government proposal would allow medication abortion from 2027.
Human Rights Watch says the rules are too restrictive and will limit safe, affordable access.
The country decriminalised abortion seven years ago but still hasn't updated the law.
stories.vc: Women's health access is also an economic issue; restrictive rules push care into costlier, riskier channels.

stories.headline: A 9-year-old girl reprogrammed a Halloween skeleton
body: Nathalie talked her parents into a $179 talking skeleton, then found it only talked about cocktails.
So she reprogrammed it with a new voice and personality; its favourite colour is now pink.
Meet 'Uncle Murray'.
stories.joke: Never underestimate a nine-year-old with a screwdriver and a plan.
stories.vc: Early hands-on tech play is how many girls get into STEM, a pipeline every tech company says it wants.
